sources.title: VAT registration threshold
sources.excerpt: You must register for VAT if either (1) your total taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over £90,000 (the rolling / backward look, checked at month-end), or (2) you expect your taxable turnover to go over £90,000 in the next 30 days alone (the forward look). You can also register voluntarily below £90,000. The former £85,000 threshold is outdated and must not be used. Confirm current figures on GOV.UK.

sources.title: VAT registration timing — rolling 12 months and 30-day forward look
sources.excerpt: Rolling 12-month (backward) test: if at the end of any month your taxable supplies in the previous 12 months (or less) exceed £90,000, you must notify HMRC within 30 days of that month-end. Effective date of registration is typically the first day of the second month after you went over the threshold. Forward-looking 30-day test: if at any time you expect taxable supplies in the next 30 days alone to exceed £90,000, you must register by the end of that 30-day period; the effective date is the date you first formed that expectation. These are separate tests — do not confuse an 11-month build-up plus next month with the forward look. Always confirm on GOV.UK / VAT Notice 700/1.

sources.title: Self Assessment late filing and payment penalties overview
sources.excerpt: If you miss Self Assessment filing or payment deadlines you may have to pay penalties and interest. Penalty amounts and timing depend on how late you are and HMRC rules for the period. Check GOV.UK Self Assessment penalties guidance for current details rather than relying on memory.
